patterns.note: Oversized, tightly-spaced sans-serif display typography that dominates the viewport, creating an urgent, editorial tone.
A brutalist grid system defined by thin, structural horizontal lines that segment the page, contrasting with chaotic, overlapping image collages.
High-contrast stark monochrome (deep black and off-white) punctuated only by the vibrant, unedited colors of user-generated social media images.
A dynamic, chaotic image scatter effect where dozens of small, square media files pile up and overlap as the user scrolls, visually simulating digital hoarding.
A horizontal 'barcode' strip of tightly packed, vertical image slivers at the bottom of the page that shifts dynamically, representing a compressed archive of saved content.

technique_notes: Recreate the brutalist editorial layout using a strict CSS grid aligned to thin, persistent horizontal borders. Use absolute positioning and z-index layering to scatter a collage of media elements across the viewport, allowing them to overlap text and each other.

Implement the digital hoarding scroll effect using GSAP ScrollTrigger or WebGL to dynamically translate, scale, and pile up dozens of small image containers as the scroll depth increases, creating a claustrophobic 'clutter' sensation.

For the bottom archive strip, slice images into narrow vertical containers within a flex row, applying a subtle hover or scroll-bound horizontal translation to expand the slices and reveal more of the underlying image.

design_tokens.type_scale: Oversized, ultra-bold display headings (~6x body size) with tight letter-spacing, contrasted against tiny, technical metadata labels in the corners.
design_tokens.spacing: Extremely airy, high-contrast negative space in text-only sections, abruptly transitioning to dense, claustrophobic, overlapping image clusters.

standout: The site brilliantly translates the abstract concept of 'digital hoarding' into a physical user experience through a chaotic, overlapping image scatter that literally clutters the screen as you scroll. It perfectly balances clean, technical brutalism with messy, human digital residue.
